draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Panaji! You're standing by Fontainhas, the old Latin quarter, with winding lanes, projecting balconies and houses painted pale yellow, green or blue under red-tiled roofs. This city was once the capital of all of Portuguese India.
draft.hungryLine: Try the native vindaloo with fish or chicken, it's hot, along with Goan sausages and fish curry rice.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk 4 minutes to the Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church above the main square, then on to the Adil Shah Palace, the oldest colonial-era building in town.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Take a slow sunset cruise on the Mandovi from beside the Captain of Ports jetty, or just wander the alleys of Fontainhas.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Panaji's Central Library, founded in 1832, says it was the first public library set up in India.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church
spots.detail: 4 min walk · Baroque church first built in 1541, with Mass in English, Konkani and Portuguese

spots.name: Adil Shah Palace
spots.detail: 8 min walk · Old summer palace of the Adil Shahi rulers, later the Old Secretariat

spots.name: Mhamai Kamat House
spots.detail: 7 min walk · 18th-century family home that was once a bead factory

tips.title: Catch the sunset cruise.
tips.body: River cruises leave from beside the Captain of Ports jetty from around sunset.

tips.title: Explore on foot.
tips.body: The best way to see Panaji is walking its alleys and taking in the Portuguese architecture.

story.title: A sultan's summer palace
story.body: The Adil Shah Palace began as a summer palace for the ruler of the Adil Shahi dynasty. It's now the oldest surviving colonial-era building in the city.

story.title: A hillside chapel
story.body: A chapel went up on a hillside overlooking Panaji in 1541. A larger church replaced it in the 1600s, and it holds a bell brought from the ruins of Old Goa.

story.title: India's first public library
story.body: The Central Library opened in the early 1830s. It says it was the first public library in India.

story.title: The 18th of June
story.body: Ram Manohar Lohia called a meeting on 18 June 1946 to end Portuguese rule. One of Panaji's busiest shopping streets, 18th June Road, is named after that day.

story.title: Goa's capital
story.body: After about 451 years, Portuguese rule ended in December 1961. Panaji, once Nova Goa, is now the capital of Goa.

food.name: Avanti Bar & Restaurant
food.detail: Right in Fontainhas, go for the vindaloo, sausages or Goan fish curry and rice

food.name: Cafe Real Tea Room
food.detail: Hot vegetarian snacks near Azad Maidan, try the bhaaji pao and onion bojjea with tea

food.name: Gujarat Lodge
food.detail: Snacks and sweets on 18th June Road, with hot samosas in the evening
